title: Hot Lips Page and Charlie Spivak
summary: He calls Page a 100 percent trumpeter and credits Spivak for his sweet playing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Yeah. That's, that was another old buddy of mine too. Yeah, he was 100 percent. I just happened to come back when he brought back Dud. I met him when I was down at 'Bama State, and then after that in New York. Yeah, a 100 percent trumpet player. And he had beautiful ideas. The same, you know, we had the growl voice all the time.
Now, you're going for a sweet man. The trumpet player that had the sweetest music and that's what he tried to do. He was living down in Greensboro, South Carolina now.

Right! Charlie Spivak. You're right. He was living out in Greensboro, South Carolina. Every December I used to drive through there. I couldn't get in touch with him. He was playing at a restaurant there. He owned part of it. But, I could never get by there to see him. I knew him through those years too. But he, I understand he retired just maybe about a year ago, just stopped ~~this~~ just about a year now. Now, that's where I like to, I try to play sweet on account of him. You know, certain tunes, during my schooling days.
